stories.headline: Ukrainian drones hit Rēzekne oil depot, triggering Defence Minister's resignation and coalition crisis
stories.summary: Two suspected Ukrainian drones entered Latvian airspace from Russia on May 7, with one striking and damaging oil storage tanks near Rēzekne in Latgale; a third drone reportedly turned back into Russia. PM Siliņa convened an emergency Crisis Management Council, publicly criticised Defence Minister Andris Sprūds (Progressives) for slow deployment of counter-drone systems and late civilian alerts, and on May 10 demanded his resignation via social media — moments before Sprūds held his own press conference announcing he was stepping down voluntarily to 'protect the army from a political campaign.' Siliņa simultaneously named army colonel Raivis Melnis, then serving as MoD representative in Ukraine, as Sprūds's replacement. The Progressives announced they would decide the following week whether to remain in the coalition; the NBS commander separately confirmed detection technology had failed. A second air-threat warning was issued overnight May 8–9 in eastern Latvia municipalities. National Alliance had already prepared a formal resignation demand before Siliņa acted, and Ukraine's foreign minister offered cooperation on drone-incident prevention.

stories.headline: Latvia celebrates 36th anniversary of independence restoration with parade and Saeima session
stories.summary: On May 4, Latvia marked 36 years since the restoration of independence with a ceremonial Saeima session and a regional military parade in Aizkraukle, the 15th time such a parade has been held in a Latvian municipality on this date. President Rinkēvičs, Defence Minister Sprūds, and NBS commanders attended and took the salute. Rinkēvičs also presented Three-Star Order decorations at Rīgas pils and issued public addresses emphasising defence investment and individual civic responsibility.

stories.headline: President Rinkēvičs makes official visit to Armenia, expresses EU integration support
stories.summary: President Edgars Rinkēvičs visited Yerevan on an official visit, meeting PM Nikol Pashinyan and President Vahagn Khachaturyan. Rinkēvičs expressed support for Armenia's aspirations to deepen ties with the European Union and invited President Khachaturyan to make a reciprocal visit to Latvia, describing the bilateral dialogue as 'excellent.'

stories.headline: Latvia receives fourth EU Recovery Fund tranche of €371 million
stories.summary: On May 8, Latvia received its fourth (penultimate) payment from the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility — €371.2 million — after fulfilling 41 plan milestones. European Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis presented the payment confirmation to PM Siliņa and Finance Minister Ašeradens; total receipts now stand at approximately €1.5 billion, or 75% of Latvia's total allocation.

stories.headline: KNAB opens probe into Šlesers campaign spending as pre-election advertising heats up
stories.summary: The Corruption Prevention Bureau (KNAB) launched a review this week into the advertising campaign of the association 'Latvija pirmā' led by Ainārs Šlesers (Latvia pirmajā vietā party), seeking to determine whether funding from a legal entity constitutes a prohibited donation to a political party. Šlesers denied wrongdoing, claiming the party name does not appear in the campaign materials; KNAB's official expressed public surprise at his claims of prior coordination with the bureau. The broader pre-election campaign landscape was also covered, with New Unity distributing a newspaper and Progressives running posters.

stories.headline: President Rinkēvičs uses suspensive veto on law altering Latvia's approach to rape definition
stories.summary: President Rinkēvičs exercised his suspensive veto to send back to parliament a law that would have changed Latvia's international commitments regarding rape definitions, arguing that such a significant change in international obligations should not be decided hastily. The veto was reported in the context of Eurostat data showing a 150% rise in recorded rape cases across the EU over the past decade, with Latvia mentioned specifically.

stories.headline: President Rinkēvičs issues Mother's Day messages across social media
stories.summary: On May 10 (Latvian Mother's Day), President Rinkēvičs published emotional tributes to mothers on Facebook and other social platforms, emphasising the importance of maternal care and encouraging mothers not to feel pressure to be 'perfect.' The messages were covered by multiple Latvian outlets.

stories.headline: Rinkēvičs and Siliņa mark Europe Day; Siliņa speech on Latvia's EU role
stories.summary: On May 9 (Europe Day), President Rinkēvičs published a formal greeting marking the 76th anniversary of the Schuman Declaration, and PM Siliņa delivered remarks at a public event, stating that Latvia is not 'a spectator of Europe' but a shaper of its future and calling EU membership one of Latvia's most important development decisions.

stories.headline: Foreign fraudsters using Latvian company names in fake job listings
stories.summary: Two Latvian outlets reported that following a parliamentary immigration investigation commission's conclusion, attention has been drawn to fraudulent job advertisements using the names of well-known Latvian companies (including brewery Aldaris) to deceive foreign nationals. The scheme appears to target people seeking work in Latvia.
